mainTopic: Using מעשר money for the חגיגה (טופל, and the dispute between חזקיה and רבי יוחנן), why מעשר בהמה is not used on יום טוב, the meaning of מסת, and which offerings fulfill the מצוה of שמחה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: whoever lets the חגיגה of the fourteenth of ניסן come from מעשר must hold that it is not a Torah obligation. Next the גמרא asks how בית הלל can allow a חגיגה from מעשר, since anything a person owes must come from חולין. עולא answers that they mean combining (טופל) מעשר with חולין. חזקיה says you combine animal with animal, and רבי יוחנן says you combine money with money. Each view is backed by a ברייתא built on the word "מסת". One ברייתא adds that on the other days of פסח even מעשר בהמה may be used. רב אשי explains that it is not allowed on יום טוב itself, because a person might come to tithe and mark animals with red dye that day. The גמרא proves from אחשורוש's tax (מס) that מסת means ordinary money. Finally it turns to the משנה's rule that ישראלים fulfill שמחה with נדרים and נדבות. A ברייתא learns this from "ושמחת בחגך", lists what כהנים may eat, and starts to exclude birds and meal offerings, with the explanation continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: So the fourteenth's חגיגה is not a Torah obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier point. Since this view allows the חגיגה of the fourteenth to come from מעשר, it must hold that this offering is not required by the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems, then, that he holds the חגיגה of the fourteenth is not a Torah obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is drawing a conclusion from the earlier discussion. Allowing מעשר money for the fourteenth's חגיגה shows that this view treats that offering as not being from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Torah obligation must be paid from חולין, not from מעשר money. So if someone lets the fourteenth's חגיגה come from מעשר, he must not see it as a Torah-level חובה. The word אלמא shows this is a logical inference, not a direct statement.

keyTerms.meaning: It seems / so we see (introduces a conclusion drawn from what came before)
He holds (this opinion)
The חגיגה offering brought on the fourteenth of ניסן together with the קרבן פסח
Not from the Torah

phrases.english: Apparently, he holds
phrases.notes: "He" is the תנא from just before, who allowed this offering to come from מעשר.

phrases.english: that the Festival offering of the fourteenth is not from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that came before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whoever allows מעשר money for the fourteenth's חגיגה treats that offering as not a Torah obligation.

steps.title: How can בית הלל allow a required offering from מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית הלל, who say a חגיגה may come from מעשר. It then asks how this can be, since anything you owe must come from חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: בית הלל say a חגיגה may come from מעשר. Why? It is an obligation, and every obligation may only come from חולין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא and then challenges it. A חגיגה is required, and required offerings must come from ordinary money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule: a חובה (something you owe) cannot be paid with מעשר שני money, only with your own חולין. The חגיגה is a required offering, so בית הלל's ruling seems to break that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: מעשר שני money or produce, which has to be used in ירושלים
Something a person is obligated to bring
Ordinary, non-holy property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "חובה" with "Torah law" here. The question is not whether the חגיגה counts. The question is which money may pay for it.

phrases.english: The Master said: Beit Hillel say:
[Festival offerings may come] from the tithe.
phrases.notes: The words in brackets aren't in the Hebrew, but they're what's meant. The "tithe" here is מעשר שני.

phrases.english: Why? It is an obligatory matter,
and any obligatory matter
comes only from non-sacred property?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר. אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting בית הלל's ruling from the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's ruling that a חגיגה may come from מעשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A required offering must come from חולין, and the חגיגה is required, so it cannot come from מעשר.

steps.title: עולא: בית הלל mean combining
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that בית הלל are talking about combining (טופל): adding מעשר money together with חולין money.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: it is a case of combining.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question. בית הלל never meant the whole offering comes from מעשר. They meant that מעשר money is added alongside חולין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With combining, the basic חובה is still covered by חולין, and מעשר only adds to it. That keeps the rule that a חובה comes from חולין. The next step gives two views on exactly how the combining works.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where one combines (adds מעשר to חולין)

phrases.english: Ulla said: [It is] where one combines.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: בית הלל are speaking only about combining.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed בית הלל allow the whole חגיגה to come from מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל only allow מעשר to be combined with חולין, so the rule that a חובה comes from חולין stays in place.

steps.title: חזקיה and רבי יוחנן disagree about how to combine
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה allows combining animal with animal but not money with money. רבי יוחנן says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: you may combine an animal with an animal, but not money with money. רבי יוחנן said: you may combine money with money, but not an animal with an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree about what "combining" means. One allows it between whole animals, and the other allows it between sums of money for one animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חזקיה, "animal with animal" means: bring one whole animal from חולין, and then extra animals may come from מעשר. Mixing the two kinds of money to buy one animal is not allowed. רבי יוחנן allows mixing the money inside one animal's purchase, but he does not allow a separate animal paid fully with מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: One may combine / attach
An animal with an animal (one whole animal from חולין, another from מעשר)
Money with money (mixing both kinds of money to buy one animal)

steps.confusionAlert: The two opinions are exact mirror images. Keep them apart: חזקיה = animals yes, money no. רבי יוחנן = money yes, animals no.
steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה: combine animal with animal, not money with money. רבי יוחנן: combine money with money, not animal with animal.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiya said: One may combine an animal with an animal,
but one may not combine money with money.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: טוֹפְלִין מָעוֹת לְמָעוֹת,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One may combine money with money,
but one may not combine an animal with an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out in two different ways what עולא's "combining" means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה allows combining animal with animal but not money with money. רבי יוחנן allows combining money with money but not animal with animal.

steps.title: Each side has a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that there is a ברייתא supporting חזקיה and another supporting רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a ברייתא like חזקיה, and there is a ברייתא like רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that both opinions have support from a תנא, and it is about to quote those sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that each side has a ברייתא means neither view gets pushed aside. Both opinions are rooted in earlier teachings, so the argument stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Ḥizkiya,
it is taught in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּחִזְקִיָּה, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Announces support for both sides of the dispute in step 4.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות, quoted in the next steps.

steps.title: The ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: From the word "מסת" we learn that a חובה comes from חולין. From "כאשר יברכך" we learn that you may mix in other money, like רבי יוחנן says.
steps.simpleTranslation: "מסת" teaches that a person brings his required offering from חולין. And how do we know that if he wants to mix, he may? Because the verse says: "as ה' your God blesses you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that backs רבי יוחנן. The verse teaches both the basic rule (חולין) and the permission to mix money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "מסת" sets the basic rule that a חובה comes from your own חולין. The words "as ה' blesses you" add that any money God has given you, even מעשר, may be mixed in. Mixing money is exactly רבי יוחנן's view of combining.

keyTerms.meaning: "The measure of" (from the verse about bringing festival offerings)
To mix (חולין money with מעשר money)
"The verse teaches" (introduces a proof from a פסוק)
"As He blesses you"

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a source in the פסוק for both halves of the rule: the חובה comes from חולין, yet extra money may be mixed in.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan:
"The measure of" teaches
that a person brings his obligatory offering from non-sacred property.
And from where [do we know] that if he wishes to mix, he may mix?
phrases.notes: "Mix" means putting his מעשר money together with his חולין money.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"As the Lord your God blesses you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the two ברייתות announced in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that money may be combined with money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading דברים 16:10: "מסת" and "כאשר יברכך ה' אלהיך".

steps.title: A teaching that supports חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a חובה comes from חולין. בית הלל say the first eating must be from חולין, and after that it may be from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא, like חזקיה: "מסת" teaches that a person brings his required offering from חולין. בית שמאי say: on the first day, from חולין; from then on, from מעשר. בית הלל say: the first eating from חולין; from then on, from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the ברייתא it promised earlier, the one that supports חזקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל speak about the first eating. That means the first animal must be from חולין, and later animals may be bought with מעשר money. This is combining animal with animal, which is exactly what חזקיה allows.

keyTerms.meaning: "according to the measure" (דברים 16:10); the word teaches that a חובה comes from חולין
the first eating, meaning the first animal eaten
from here on, after that point
here, money of מעשר שני

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the ברייתא in step 6. That one supported רבי יוחנן (money with money). This one supports חזקיה (animal with animal).

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא, in line with חזקיה:
"According to the measure":

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁאָדָם מֵבִיא חוֹבָתוֹ מִן הַחוּלִּין,
phrases.english: teaches that a person brings his required offering from non-holy property.
בית שמאי say:
On the first day, from non-holy property;
from then on, from the tithe.
And בית הלל say:
The first eating must be from non-holy property;
phrases.notes: In other words, the first animal you eat. That is why this supports חזקיה, who combines animal with animal.

phrases.english: from then on, from the tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן, the גמרא brings the second one, which supports חזקיה.
steps.raayaObject: חזקיה's view that you may combine animal with animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which בית הלל say "the first eating from חולין, after that from מעשר"

steps.title: On the rest of פסח, even מעשר בהמה works
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: on the other days of פסח, a person can fulfill his obligation even with מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on all the other days of פסח, a person fulfills his obligation with מעשר בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and adds a new rule about the rest of פסח. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "the other days" implies that on the first day of יום טוב, מעשר בהמה does not work. The ברייתא does not give a reason, so the גמרא will ask for one.

keyTerms.meaning: the tithe of animals, where every tenth animal becomes holy
fulfills his obligation
the other days of פסח, after the first day

phrases.english: And on all the other days of Pesach,
a person fulfills his obligation
with animal tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the days of פסח after the first, one may fulfill his obligation with מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: Why not on the first day of יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why מעשר בהמה cannot be used on the first day of יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: On יום טוב, what is the reason it is not allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple "why" question about the ברייתא's last line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allowed מעשר בהמה only on the other days. The גמרא wants to know what is different about the first day of יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
the festival day itself, here the first day of פסח

phrases.english: On יום טוב, what is the reason it is not allowed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks for the reason behind the rule in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why מעשר בהמה may not be used for the obligation on the first day of יום טוב

steps.title: You might come to tithe on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that a person might tithe his animals on יום טוב, and that is forbidden because of the red dye used to mark the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Maybe he will come to tithe on יום טוב, and you cannot tithe on יום טוב because of the red dye.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מעשר בהמה were allowed on the first day, someone who runs out of animals might separate the tithe right then. Separating the tithe means marking the tenth animal with red dye, which is not allowed on יום טוב. So the חכמים blocked using it at all on that day.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps, maybe (a worry)
to separate the tithe
red dye used to mark the tenth animal

steps.whatToRemember: On the first day of יום טוב you may not use מעשר בהמה, as a fence, so you won't come to tithe and mark animals on יום טוב.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
Perhaps he will come to separate the tithe on יום טוב,
and it is impossible to tithe on יום טוב
because of the red dye.
phrases.notes: Every tenth animal was marked with red paint, and marking like that is not allowed on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לְעַשּׂוֹרֵי בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a protective rule: one might tithe on יום טוב, which is forbidden because of marking with red dye.

steps.title: How do we know מסת means חולין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the word מסת and asks how we know it refers to non-holy property.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we see that this word מסת is a term for חולין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the word מסת from the ברייתות and asks for proof of what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות relied on מסת to teach that a חובה comes from חולין. The גמרא now wants to know why this word points to ordinary money.

keyTerms.meaning: how do we see it? where is it implied?
a term, a way of speaking

phrases.english: From where is it understood that this "מסת"
is a term for non-holy property?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי מִסַּת לִישָּׁנָא דְחוּלִּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side question about יום טוב, the גמרא goes back to the derivation from מסת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the word מסת means חולין

steps.title: Proof from King אחשורוש's tax
steps.stepSummary: The word מס is used for the tax אחשורוש put on the land, and a king's tax is plain, non-holy money.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And King אחשורוש put a tax on the land."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from מגילת אסתר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אסתר, מס means a king's tax, which is ordinary money. So מסת in the תורה is understood the same way: the offering comes from your own regular money, חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: a tax, tribute
the king in מגילת אסתר

steps.whatToRemember: מסת is read like מס, a tax, which is ordinary money. That is why a חובה must come from חולין.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And King אחשורוש placed
a tax upon the land."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וַיָּשֶׂם הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ מַס עַל הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מס in אסתר means a king's tax, which is ordinary money, so מסת means חולין.

steps.title: Returning to the משנה: ישראלים fulfill their obligation with vow and gift offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה: ישראלים fulfill their obligation of שמחה with נדרים and נדבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: ישראלים fulfill their obligation with vow offerings and gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can discuss it next. This is a setup step that opens the topic for the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was discussing the word מסת. Now it turns to a different line of the משנה. That line says a person does not need a special new animal for שלמי שמחה, because his נדרים and נדבות can count.

keyTerms.meaning: their obligation (literally: the hands of their obligation)
vow offerings, where a person says 'I take upon myself to bring an offering'
gift offerings, where a person says 'this animal is an offering'

phrases.english: Israelites fulfill their obligation
phrases.notes: This is the obligation to eat שלמי שמחה, the rejoicing offerings, on the חג.

phrases.english: with vow offerings and gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצְאִין יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן בִּנְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of מסת and opens a new line from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראלים can fulfill שמחה with their נדרים and נדבות.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the פסוק includes all kinds of rejoicing for ישראלים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "ושמחת בחגך" that all types of rejoicing count. From here, ישראלים fulfill their obligation with נדרים, נדבות and מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "And you shall rejoice in your feast" comes to include every kind of rejoicing as rejoicing. From here the חכמים said: ישראלים fulfill their obligation with vow offerings, gift offerings and animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the source for the משנה's rule. The source is the פסוק "ושמחת בחגך".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוק broadly. It teaches that you do not need one particular kind of offering for the מצוה of שמחה. That is why the ברייתא adds מעשר בהמה to the משנה's list of נדרים and נדבות.

keyTerms.meaning: and you shall rejoice in your feast
to include
from here they said

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the משנה's rule about נדרים ונדבות comes from a פסוק, and that the list is wider than the משנה spelled out.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And you shall rejoice in your feast"
comes to include all kinds of rejoicing as rejoicing.
From here the Sages said:
Israelites fulfill their obligation
with vow offerings, gift offerings, and animal tithe,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the משנה's rule and adds מעשר בהמה to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "ושמחת בחגך" includes all types of rejoicing, so ישראלים can use נדרים, נדבות and מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: What the כהנים can use for rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: כהנים fulfill their obligation with חטאת, אשם, בכור, and the חזה ושוק of שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the כהנים fulfill their obligation with sin offerings, guilt offerings, firstborn animals, and the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and lists what the כהנים can eat to fulfill the מצוה of שמחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are parts of offerings that only כהנים eat. Since the פסוק includes all kinds of rejoicing, the meat that belongs to the כהנים also counts for them.

keyTerms.meaning: sin offering
guilt offering
firstborn animal, given to the כהן
the breast and thigh of a שלמים, given to the כהן

phrases.english: And the priests with sin offerings, guilt offerings, and firstborn animals,
and with the breast and thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from ישראלים to כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים fulfill שמחה with חטאת, אשם, בכור, and חזה ושוק.

steps.title: Could birds and meal offerings also count? The פסוק says no
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that maybe even bird offerings and meal offerings could count, and answers by quoting "ושמחת בחגך" again.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that even bird offerings and meal offerings count. So the פסוק says: "And you shall rejoice in your feast."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: since 'all kinds of rejoicing' count, maybe עופות and מנחות count too. It rejects that idea with the same פסוק. How this פסוק shows it is explained on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that widened the list now also sets its limit. The word 'all' does not mean every offering. Exactly which word in the פסוק excludes עופות and מנחות is explained on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: one might think (introduces an idea that will be rejected)
bird offerings
meal offerings, made of flour
therefore the פסוק says (brings a פסוק to answer)

steps.confusionAlert: The same פסוק was just used to include more offerings. Here it is used to exclude some. The ברייתא is not contradicting itself. The next amud explains which detail in the פסוק sets the limit.

phrases.english: One might think even with bird offerings and meal offerings —
therefore the verse says: "And you shall rejoice in your feast,"

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף בָּעוֹפוֹת וּבִמְנָחוֹת תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the wide inclusion taught in steps 14 and 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that עופות and מנחות can fulfill the מצוה of שמחה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'All kinds of rejoicing' does not mean every type of offering. The פסוק itself limits it, and the explanation comes on the next amud.
